result.summary:
The only part that failed audit 1 was R group 4 (head +0.88, soundness 2), so it is the only part rewritten. Slots a and b and R1 to R3 passed and are byte-identical; a diff against the backup at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-AlphaCube/84cd2fa5-62ee-4d6f-b035-b604567ee88d/scratchpad/missions_r2_attempt1.yaml confirms it.

R4 change: I dropped the two variants that swapped the pool variable for nominal price and for the cumulative adjustment factor. The auditor found that y was still in adjusted-price units, so the split could not be read. Both variants also had |rho| < 0.27 with the head, so they would have been added as new heads rather than replacing a bad part. The nominal-price pool also came close to trap 3.

Following the auditor's first step, R4 now has one variant that replaces only the ranking quantity y with its scale-free form:
`sub(cs_first_low20(abs_(div(day_wstd(Vwap, High), day_mean(Vwap))), pow_3(day_mean(Open))), ts_var(day_gini(High), 10))`
The pool, abs_ and the ts_var tail are unchanged.

Evidence and expectations in the why field:
- y alone scores -1.06 / -0.39 in the sufficiency test, almost the same as price alone at -1.16 / -0.45, so y is mostly reading price level.
- Inside the cheapest-20% pool, the price factor in y pushes the long book toward the pool's more expensive end, the opposite of the pool's direction.
- Counter-evidence: head +0.65 uses the same smoothed-price pool with a scale-free y (day_corr) and scores 0.11 below the comparable original version (+0.76).
- I put the chance of clearing the +0.978 replacement line at about 15%, and expect rho with the original head of 0.6 to 0.8.
- Criteria set in advance: if vol |rho| >= 0.45, rho with the original head < 0.5, or the gain appears in only one of train and valid, the group should not pass.
- The pool split moves to round 3, and only if this step does not lose score.
